title: Pull-Out Kitchen Faucet Replacement: Replacement of old faucet, valves, and under-sink plumbing

locations.name: Basement shut-off area (water supply)
locations.basis: Transcript notes turning water off in the basement.

locations.name: Under-sink installation area (kitchen cabinet)</name>
locations.basis: Installation activities occur under the kitchen sink, including mounting plate and valve work.

summary: This Old House guides a kitchen faucet replacement focused on a pull-out spray faucet. The video walks through diagnosing a leaking, aging faucet, previewing a new stainless model with a higher spout and pull-out spray, and then performing the upgrade: turning off water at the basement shut-offs, removing the old faucet with a basin wrench, preparing the sink with plumber’s putty, installing a new base plate, replacing under-sink shut-off valves with compression fittings, mounting the new faucet, attaching the spray hose and its weight, and finally testing hot/cold operation and the spray/soap dispenser functions. Along the way, it contrasts soldered versus compression connections and demonstrates practical under-sink hardware like bending springs and clip hardware.
topics: Emery cloth cleaning of valve connections
Mounting bracket and special tightening tool
Rigid copper supply lines with bending spring
Testing for leaks and proper operation

sections.title: Assess old faucet and plan
sections.description: The host assesses a 30-year-old kitchen faucet and sink, noting leaking issues and ambitions for a taller spout and a pull-out spray (plus a soap dispenser). Observations about the under-sink area begin the diagnostic step before replacing components.

sections.title: Preview new faucet and prep for replacement
sections.description: A stainless-finish pull-out faucet is introduced, highlighting the higher spout and retractable spray hose, and mentioning the addition of a matching soap dispenser as part of the upgrade plan.

sections.title: Shut-off planning and space preparation
sections.description: The plan includes locating and turning off the basement shut-off valves, moving the disposer to gain space, and preparing the under-sink area for the new faucet installation.

sections.title: Remove old faucet and prepare mounting area
sections.description: Old faucet nuts are removed with a basin wrench; supply lines are cut and removed, and the base area for the new faucet is prepped with plumber’s putty to seal the mounting plate.

sections.title: Valve cleanup and soldering note
sections.description: Old shut-off connections are unsoldered and cleaned; the video notes that the new valves use compression fittings (with a brass nut and ferrule) instead of soldering, illustrating the transition in the plumbing upgrade.

sections.title: Mounting the new faucet and hose hardware
sections.description: The faucet is threaded through the base plate, anchored beneath the sink with a mounting bracket, a clip is installed for the spray hose, and a weight is mounted to help retract the hose.

sections.title: Final connections and test
sections.description: Water is reconnected and the system is tested: confirming hot on the left, cold on the right, pulling out the spray, and testing the soap dispenser functionality to ensure all functions operate correctly.

featured_techniques.technique: Pull-out kitchen faucet installation with base plate, mounting bracket, and spray hose
Use of plumber's putty around the base plate to seal under-sink mounting
Compression valve installation (no soldering) using ferrule
Basin wrench to remove old faucet nuts
Spray hose path, clip installation, and weight mounting
Rigid copper supply lines formed with bending spring to prevent kinking
Final test of hot/cold operation and spray/soap dispenser
